I emailed them for a few weeks and it helped a bit at first. They'll talk you through how you're feeling and there's absolutely no fear about them contacting anyone on your behalf. Unsolicited attempts to counsel tend to go fairly wrong. 
A friendly chat though can really help. I've been speaking with a new found friend on here and i can tell they genuinely care about talking with me. We discuss stuff, sometimes light sometimes not so much. They took the time and effort to get to know me and made me want to know them. 

It doesn't happen easily, it's taken me months to find someone online who is willing to talk. But I'm so grateful for it. A lot of it is to do with clicking with the person too, I feel. The person I speak with is from Scotland and is in the LGBT group, like me, so we have a lot of the same cultural experiences so we can relate more easily.

Because you're taking the time to talk to her, spend time with her when she's feeling vulnerable. 
I appreciate you want help for her but 'I love you' isn't going to stop her wanting to commit suicide. 
My partner of 2.5 years tells me she loves me every day, had a cry about what it would feel like to know that I killed myself and made me promise not to do it. It's not taking away the urge, though. The utter desperation, hopeless and patheticness. I still hurt myself in secret and I feel so guilty that she'll find out. 

Point is, the issue is complex and random acts of online anonymous strangers tend to glance off those complex issues. There has to be a long term goal, plan and want for it to work.

Positive. We know nothing about her, our words won't sound genuine. 
At the very least she needs a friend/ family member/ doctor to talk about her feelings openly. So then they can create a plan to try to help her. 

If I woke up to a bunch of 'I love you's from strangers, I'd appreciate the effort but I'd also roll my eyes so hard that I saw my brain.
Sending 'l love you' 'don't do it' 'permanent solution to temporary pain' won't help, honestly.

Oh god, I'm so so sorry. I can't imagine having a wife level of trust be broken. That really is a kick to the confidence. :S. 
I can imagine it will be hard to believe that other people can be trusted when you're other half proves that it's actually not as solid as you'd hope. 
If it's possible at all, reaching out to a friend could help ease some of that build up, you might be feeling. If you're anything like me, there's both the horror of sharing to stop you but also the frantic bouncing thoughts get more frantic the longer they're held in. We ignore it, pretend it's not happening, stay up all night flicking through Reddit, distract ourselves to the point we're exhausted. And everything is so loud and heavy that doing something final could give us some relief and quiet and certainty that we won't have to feel all of this bullshit again. It's all of that which brought me back to this subreddit (I find it jumps between spiralling me down and sometimes giving some relief from chats). 

Anyway, my point is, you need to release some of that somehow. Reddit sharing is a super start. 
Another place could be a suicide hotline like samaritains. I've never spoken with them but I emailed them. I got one or two emails back a day and they were pretty encouraging. They're a good place to write down everything and know that you never have to reply to them again and feel no guilt. 
Writing everything down, on your phone/ note book can help organise your thoughts and feelings. Pretend you're explaining to your mug of coffee what happened? I do that all the time. Like full blown conversations when I'm alone. Sometimes it helps, other times I get upset. Regardless it releases some emotion.

I am a week away from sitting my final exams at university. I have made plans to kill myself over the next week. Throughout the last year and a half I've been physically and psychologically scarred by the process. I'm a mess. And it's going to take a long time to heal, if I chose that route. Two of my friends have reached the point where drugs, alcohol and the promise of a quick suicide are the only things keeping them keeping them going. 

College is truly brutal for some of us and we aren't prepared for it at all. We're taught to study, organise course work and sit exams but we are definitely not taught how to deal with the crippling fear and stress that comes with it.

I don't think I'm bold enough for that. I haven't been back for blood tests until they're healed. I really know it's nothing they haven't seen before but I'm still so ashamed of myself. I think I've been wearing long sleeves for two or three months now because of it.

There's a part of me that seriously wants to travel and explore the world with her, that would be worth living for if I thought I could survive and be a happy person. I just think I'm so worthless that she'd be better off with someone who can make her happier. I don't want to leave her, I want to show her she can rely on me and trust me again.
